Subject: Air-gapped private deployment — HW checklist, upgrade windows, and SLA clarifications

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so everyone has the same view:

- Goal: Proof-of-concept (3–6 months) for on-prem, air-gapped deployment of Redwood Private in Acme Health data centers. Primary workloads: clinical note generation and de-identified embeddings for research.
- Top risks you flagged: hardware procurement lead times, coordinated OS/firmware patching in an air-gapped environment, and maintenance/upgrade windows for the LLM runtime.

Action items we committed to:
1) I will send a lightweight HW checklist (attached) that maps minimum and recommended GPU configs to expected tokens/sec for typical Acme prompts.
2) Vivek will follow up with specifics on offline upgrade procedures and what binary/artifact handoff looks like for air-gapped installs.
3) Acme to confirm expected RTO/RPO and which maintenance windows are acceptable (weekend vs nightly).

Two clarifying questions for you now so we can tailor the checklist and service-level discussions:
- Do you have an internal policy on allowed vendor-supplied images or do we need to provide fully signed, hashed artifacts for offline install?
- Preferred cadence for security patching (monthly baseline vs ad-hoc emergency)?

Attached: redwood_private_hw_checklist.xlsx (short table: recommended SKUs, NIC requirements, swap/ephemeral disk guidance) and proposal_v2.pdf (commercials for Dedicated vs Private).

I'll loop back once Vivek confirms the offline upgrade MOP.

Best,

Hi Monica —

Thanks for the summary and attachments. A few answers and follow-ups from our side:

- Artifact policy: We require vendor images to be signed and accompanied by SHA256 checksums. We can host the artifacts on an internal artifactory that only accepts signed uploads.
- Patch cadence: security patches are triaged weekly; OS/firmware updates happen quarterly unless it's a CVE; we would expect the vendor to provide emergency hotfixes.
- Maintenance windows: preferred is Saturday 02:00–06:00 local time for major upgrades; minor patches can be applied in 01:00–03:00 weekday windows if needed.

Two technical asks before we set an internal approval meeting:
1) Can Redwood provide an offline upgrade MOP that shows step-by-step how the runtime is updated without internet access and how to validate KV cache integrity post-upgrade?
2) For hardware: do you support multi-node KV cache replication or is persistence based solely on local SSD snapshots? We need to understand failure recovery at node-level.

If you can get Vivek to respond to 1 & 2, we'll lock a review with our security and infra leads next week.

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer | Acme Health

Subject: Re: Air-gapped private deployment — HW checklist, upgrade windows, and SLA clarifications

Jordan —

Longer answers below, plus a short MOP outline attached in-body (we'll formalize in a separate doc):

1) Offline upgrade MOP (high level):
- Prework: vendor sends signed artifact bundle + checksums to Acme via approved secure channel (we also support physical media shipment if required).
- Validation: Acme performs checksum verification and verifies vendor GPG signature.
- Staging: Install onto a non-production node in your cluster; run integration smoke tests (we provide a test harness that runs locally — no outbound required).
- KV cache handling: before upgrade, we snapshot local SSD cache to a new snapshot file. During upgrade we preserve snapshot blob; on first start the runtime runs a cache rehydration step with consistency checks (checksum of persisted segments). If rehydration fails, runtime falls back to cold start; we'll provide tooling to replay KV segments if needed.
- Rollback: we maintain prior runtime image on disk for quick rollback and include automated health checks to validate token-throughput and latency after switch.

2) KV replication and persistence: currently Redwood Private supports local SSD snapshots + an optional intra-cluster replication plugin that can replicate persisted segments over the private management network. For fully air-gapped installs we recommend SSD snapshots + periodic encrypted tape/portable-SSD export for cross-node recovery. Multi-node synchronous replication is supported but requires cluster network configuration (we documented bandwidth and latency expectations in the attached checklist).

3) Hardware notes (high level):
- Minimum: 2x A5000-class GPUs (8–12GB each) for a basic inference node; recommended: 4x A100/80GB or equivalent for production throughput.
- NIC: 25Gbps minimum recommended for replication lanes; 100Gbps for high-throughput clusters.
- Disk: NVMe 1TB for runtime/cache; separate 4TB SATA for archived snapshots.

4) SLA implications: air-gapped private installs can have a higher MTTR for emergency patching (physical artifact delivery) unless local air-gapped artifact hosting is established. If Acme hosts the artifact repo internally we can commit to a 24–48hr emergency response window plus remote diagnostics via Redacted-signed support bundles.

Attachments referenced: inline MOP outline (we will produce a formal PDF).

Next step: Monica, would you please propose two times for a technical run-through next week (Vivek + Jordan + Acme infra + Redwood infra) so we can walk the checklist and validate the artifact handoff process?

Cheers,
